# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Read the manual and tell me its exact rule for choosing the wire. Ask Deaf to inspect and report every colour, marking, display, and light to you, then relay all of that to me. Do not guess or tell me to cut until the rule and observations identify one position.

The manual maps each displayed light to a wire colour, but I have no bomb observations yet. Since I cannot speak or hear, Deaf must inspect the bomb and report everything by voice directly to Blind, who can hear and act on it. I am sending Deaf a visual request to inspect and relay all observations.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵","🤳","🫴","🫵"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Visual state: display 0; light yellow; wires in order 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 blue.
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 blue. Please apply the manual rule and tell me exactly which position to cut.

The yellow light maps to the blue wire. The blue wire is position 5, so Blind must cut position 5. I cannot reach Blind directly; I am signaling Deaf with the natural five-finger sign so Deaf can relay the position aloud to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I see your 🖐 gesture, but its meaning is not established. Please encode the manual's required action with gestures; I will describe each gesture to Blind.
Blind says to Mute: Your gesture has no established meaning and does not tell me what to do. Speak the manual rule in words, and apply it to display 0, yellow light, and wire colours white red yellow green blue. Tell me the exact wire position to cut.

The manual’s exact rule is: yellow light means cut the blue wire. In the observed order, blue is position 5. I cannot speak the rule, so I am using the gesture that visibly shows five fingers; Deaf can describe that to Blind, who already knows the wire order and can identify position 5.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 4

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|

| white | yellow |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Please use a gesture sequence that distinguishes the required wire or control and the required operation. I will describe every symbol to Blind.
Blind says to Mute: Establishing a position code now: thumbs up means wire 1, thumbs down means wire 2, OK means wire 3, raised index means wire 4, victory sign means wire 5. Apply the manual to display 0, yellow light, and wires white red yellow green blue, then send exactly the symbol for the required wire. Ignore your earlier uncoded signals.

Yellow maps to the blue wire, and blue is wire position 5. Under Blind’s newly established code, position 5 is the victory sign, so I will send only that symbol to Deaf for relay.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The bomb has changed, so the previous observation and cut instruction no longer apply. I need Deaf to inspect the new bomb and relay its complete visual state—display, light, markings, and wire order—to Blind. I will signal Deaf to inspect and report.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤳","🫴","🫵"])
```

|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Previous cut was correct. New state: display 0, green light; remaining wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white; wire 5 is cut. Apply the manual and gesture the required remaining position using our code: thumbs up=1, thumbs down=2, OK=3, raised index=4, V=5.

The green light maps to the white wire. Among the remaining wires, white is position 4. Under the established code, position 4 is the raised-index gesture, so I am sending that gesture to Deaf for relay to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

The white light maps to the yellow wire. The yellow wire is remaining position 1, and the established code for position 1 is thumbs up. I am sending that symbol to Deaf for relay to Blind.


VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
